atoms.b: Brass instruments are made of ((++metal wood)). More precisely, they are made of brass. Brass is an alloy, or mixture, of copper and zinc. It is often used for jewellery or musical instruments. Brass is easily bent and provides a good ((++tone bone)).

instruction.text: Which metal is a trumpet made from?

trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.

atoms.text: Brass instruments belong to the wider wind instrument family. A sound is produced when you blow into the mouthpiece with pursed lips. The sound is amplified by the mouthpiece and travels into the tube.
Brass instruments are constructed differently from woodwind instruments and differ in shape. Here, a trumpet (brass) and an oboe (woodwind) are shown for comparison.
atoms.sound: Brass instruments are constructed differently from woodwind instruments and differ in shape. Here, a trumpet and an oboe are shown for comparison.

atoms.a: Which instrument has a curved tube?

instruction.text: Select the tube of the instrument described.

atoms.a: In the case of the tuba, the sound tube is particularly long and wound several times.
The French horn also has a sound tube wound several times.
The sound tube of the trumpet is also coiled. However, it is smaller.
The sound tube of the trombone is the only one that is not rolled, but s-shaped.

atoms.b: If you were to unwind the sound tubes, you could measure their actual ((++lengths weights)). These lengths vary considerably. The length of the sound tube determines the ((++pitch volume)) of the instrument.
The tuba has the ((++longest shortest)) tube and the ((++lowest highest)) pitch. Next come the trombone, followed by the horn. The trumpet has the ((++shortest longest)) tube.
